title: bug: Approved epic rail is silently truncated at 1000 characters
description:
Approved proposal prop-d3ccceade25f4af19518ce0e930e4123 retains the full R07 size exception and QA-required probe allowance, but allRails.epic and persisted epic-fe5e32c32b044a20944c693dfd79411b.epicRails cut it at exactly 1000 characters, ending scripts/local-runner/guest-b.
Repro: compare the HUMAN-approved proposedValue (2026-10-25T07:43:43Z) with moe.get_context for task-84c2da018ce74995b609805dab4fe7da; required safety restrictions and the approved growth allowance are missing. Preserve approved rail text or reject oversize proposals before approval; repair existing truncated rail via Moe.
reopenReason: Per amend-1 / comment-f610453a: human chose "Raise limit; preserve longer rails" after steps 1-4, so the 1000-unit ceiling is obsolete (proposed 10000 UTF-16 units, reject-not-truncate kept). NOT calling complete_task. Steps 1-5 are COMPLETED and bytes are preserved in the worktree (uncommitted, all reported in modifiedFiles): validators.ts (MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS=1000 constant; validateStringArrayValue trailing truncate=true param; epicRails passes false), proposeRail.ts (EPIC ADD/MODIFY prevalidation before createProposal; REMOVE/GLOBAL/TASK untouched), proposeRail.test.ts (15 lossless-boundary cases), validators.test.ts (3 truncate-option cases), docs/SCHEMA.md (Epic rail limits). Evidence at 1000 cap, native-Linux snapshot of HEAD 759cc61 + overlays: npm test exit 0, 159 files/3768 passed/15 skipped, tsc 0; mutation probes (restore truncation, drop prevalidation, validate REMOVE, validate all scopes, flip default) all RED. Moving to 10000 is small: change the one constant; update proposeRail.test.ts `LIMIT = 1000` and the literal 1000 mentions in SCHEMA.md; add a real 1650-unit single-entry test plus a >10000 refusal test; then a fresh full gate. Heads-up: (1) epic rails ride in every get_context twice (epic.epicRails and allRails.epic), so a larger cap raises every task's token cost; (2) createEpic still truncates at 1000 via sanitizeStringArray, filed as task-6b607b1278914531a75bfe16decf3199 (depends on this task); (3) recombining the three restored slices into one rail must wait for a daemon restart on the new build. Details in Serena memory task-task-ab6aac94d9424653bb45d6db4fa3fe67-handoff.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
# Lossless epic rail validation
Goal: refuse unrepresentable EPIC rail changes before review and never silently shorten human-approved constraints. Architecture: reuse validateStringValue and add an opt-out to the existing array truncation behavior only at validateEpicUpdates; propose_rail shares the same cap. TypeScript/Node/Vitest. Raising the cap would merely postpone silent truncation and broaden policy; retaining the established 1000 bound with explicit refusals is the minimal compatible fix.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Root cause confirmed: validateStringArrayValue unconditionally passes truncate:true; validateEpicUpdates calls it for epicRails with 1000. proposeRail accepts any proposed string. StateManager.approveProposal calls applyRailChange before persisting APPROVED, and the EPIC branch calls updateEpic -> validateEpicUpdates, so one strict store validator also protects old pending proposals. GLOBAL/TASK apply paths intentionally preserve long rails; StateManager.test.ts has a >1000 global rule regression. No need to edit StateManager. Runtime repair already performed by architect via moe.update_epic using exact approved slices (419/432/799), not source editing or a new waiver.
planningNotes.risks: Keep the shared array validator's existing default behavior for its other callers; only epicRails opts into rejection. Length uses JS string.length, not UTF-8 bytes or code points. At 100-item boundary a later approval can legitimately refuse due to newer rails; never mark a failed apply APPROVED. Don't promise transaction rollback across epic and subsequent proposal writes. DoD has only a placeholder and no architect MCP update tool: concrete criteria recorded in comment-47c11f2a0a9a4a6bb19539857c296764 and governor notified via msg-d6996dd217774f5c95f9ff72645d7d7e. No unanswered question blocks this TURBO plan.

implementationPlan.description: Add focused lossless-rail regressions first (test-driven-development), reusing ToolTestHarness in this file. For EPIC ADD_RAIL and MODIFY_RAIL, proposedValue length 1001 must throw INVALID_INPUT before createProposal, leave proposals/map/files/activity/events unchanged; length 1000 must survive proposal, real approveProposal and state.load byte-for-byte, including leading/trailing whitespace and Unicode. Example boundary assertion: `const rail = 'x'.repeat(999) + 'Z'; ... expect(h.state.getEpic('epic-1')!.epicRails).toContain(rail);`. Seed a legacy PENDING oversized EPIC proposal directly through state.createProposal and call the real approval path; assert it stays PENDING, both proposal and epic files/cache remain identical, and no PROPOSAL_APPROVED/EPIC_UPDATED event appears. Exercise direct updateEpic with a valid first rail and oversized second rail, then with non-string/blank/NUL/newline values: fail the entire update without partial changes. Keep existing trailing-whitespace lookup assertions. Add compatibility controls for GLOBAL and TASK rails longer than 1000 and REMOVE_RAIL with empty proposedValue; never cap currentValue, so historic long rails remain removable.

implementationPlan.description: Fix the actual lossy boundary with the smallest shared validation change. Export MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS = 1000 from validators.ts; let validateStringArrayValue accept an optional truncation flag defaulting to its existing true behavior, and have validateEpicUpdates use false ONLY for epicRails. Example: `validateStringArrayValue(input.epicRails, 'epicRails', 100, MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS, false)` with the option fed into validateStringValue; preserve unrelated attribution.exclude/appendOnlyFiles sanitization and every existing item-count/type/empty/control-character rule. In proposeRail.handler, before createProposal and publication, validate proposedValue for EPIC ADD_RAIL/MODIFY_RAIL with `validateStringValue(params.proposedValue, 'proposedValue', {maxLength: MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS})`; retain the original exact string, no trim/truncate/coercion. Document the conditional EPIC bound in the schema property's description rather than imposing a universal maxLength that would break GLOBAL/TASK compatibility. REMOVE_RAIL uses only currentValue and must not validate its unused proposedValue as a replacement. Error handling: oversize or malformed new text returns INVALID_INPUT with the field, no proposal write. Existing pending proposals and direct epic writes hit validateEpicUpdates before writeEntity, so approval fails before approveProposal marks it APPROVED; do not add a second write, migration, StateManager refactor or client change. Verify first-epic-write failure also leaves the proposal pending via an injected writeEntity failure. Keep changes and tests below 400 net LOC.
implementationPlan.note: validators.ts: exported MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS=1000; validateStringArrayValue gained a trailing truncate=true param (default preserves attribution.exclude/appendOnlyFiles behavior); validateEpicUpdates passes false for epicRails only. proposeRail.ts: EPIC ADD/MODIFY proposals run validateStringValue(proposedValue, {maxLength: MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS}) before any write (exact string kept; REMOVE_RAIL, GLOBAL, TASK untouched); schema description documents the conditional bound. No StateManager change: approveProposal -> applyRailChange -> updateEpic -> validateEpicUpdates refuses before writeEntity so legacy oversized PENDING proposals stay PENDING.
